newsitem.title: FINLAND: ENSO SELLS CHEMICAL UNIT TO AKZO.
newsitem.headline: ENSO SELLS CHEMICAL UNIT TO AKZO.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy said in a statement on Thursday it will sell its paper chemicals unit Enso Paperikemia Oy to Eka Chemicals, part of the Dutch Akzo Nobel group.
Enso did not give the price of the deal, but said it would book a profit of about 450 million markka from the sale.
"Enso has sold the entire business operations of its Oulu-based subsidiary Enso Paperikemia to Eka Chemicals," Enso said.
"The sale is part of Enso's strategy programme in which resources are being increasingly channelled into developing the group's paper and board business," it said.
Enso Paperikemia's annual net sales are around 400 million markka (roughly 150 million guilders) and Enso said the unit was profitable and its business was growing.

The sale of Paperikemia together with Enso's pull-out last year from another forest industry chemicals unit, Forchem Oy, had "released around one billion markka in capital from the group's forest chemical business," Enso said.
Enso said its consumption of paper chemicals, especially latex for use in paper coating, would increase when its new fine paper machine being built in Oulu comes on stream this summer.

"Enso will remain an important customer for the paper chemicals plants in Oulu...Akzo Nobel and its partners have good prospects for further developing operations at the Oulu plant," Enso said. -- Helsinki Newsroom +358 9 680 50 24
